Commentary.Commentary: Right then! India have dominated in both Tests so far which is not a surprise given their performance at home. However the Kiwis have fought hard in each match which actually compels us to view the third Test in Indore, the first of such format at that venue. Can the Kiwis offer a fight and earn a draw or a win? Or will India complete a whitewash? Join us on Saturday, 8th October, 2016 at 0930 IST (0400 GMT) for the final Test of the series. Until then, Adios! Take Care!

Victorious Indian captain, VIRAT KOHLI says that it was a brilliant Test cricket wicket, apart from the variable bounce here and there. Feels that it was a complete all-round performance by the team. Opines that the runs added by the lower order in the first innings were crucial. Also says that he expected New Zealand to come out hard and praises his team for showing character. Feels Saha is one of the best in the country in terms of keeping and adds that his knock in the West Indies has given him confidence and now he understands how to play with the tail. Feels that Indian batsmen threw their wickets away in the first innings but in the second, the Kiwis bowled well. Struts that he is not surprised with Rohit's knock as he expected him to continue his love affair with Eden and score big at least once. Praises the crowd as he reckons that half the time, the players' confidence rose because of them, especially when a fast bowler like Shami comes running in. On the team regaining the number 1 ranking, he says that retaining the same is difficult and it all comes to how the team responds when put under pressure.

New Zealand skipper, ROSS TAYLOR is very impressed with his bowlers who put India under pressure in hot and humid circumstances. Praises Saha and the Indian lower order who played well in both innings. On the pitch, he says that he expected a different wicket but also says that it is a good one. It supported the faster bowlers but if the spinners landed the ball in the right areas, they had some purchase. Feels that after conceding a lead of around 112, they were always behind. They started well with the ball but could not sustain the pressure and feels Rohit took the game away. On the final Test, he feels they have nothing to lose and hopes his team does well in Indore where most of his players have never been. On Kane Williamson's availability for the third Test, he is pleased to see his skipper at the ground today and hopes that he recovers in the next few days before the Indore Test.

WRIDDHIMAN SAHA has been named the Man Of The Match. He scored twin half centuries in the match and his wicket-keeping was brilliant. Saha says that he is happy on winning the series and the Man Of The Match award. Thanks the crowd for supporting him. Says that there was no pressure on him and he was just concentrating on rotating the strike and putting the bad balls away. Feels that the Kolkata media support every player and he is one of them. Adds that he took some time to play on this track as it was difficult from the Kanpur pitch. On wicketkeeping, the modest guy says that he just did his job behind the stumps, nothing much. On asked to detail, he adds that he just watched the ball till the last moment and tried to collect with soft hands.

Plenty to learn for New Zealand from this Test. They were on top a couple of times but failed to capitalize. The bowling has done okay, picking up 20 wickets but the batting flopped big time. Only one batsman managed to cross the half century mark in both innings combined and they lacked big partnerships. They missed Kane Williamson dearly. Stay tuned for the presentation.

So a good performance from India but was it that clinical? Nope, perhaps. In both innings with the bat, they lost their top order cheaply and their middle order rescued them. Then, some vital runs from the lower order changed the momentum. No issues with the bowling front - every bowler performed well.

Ashwin got rid of Latham immediately after Tea and then a procession followed. Wickets kept tumbling one after the another as the Kiwis lost 7/56 in 27.4 overs. A team effort it was as Shami, Ashwin and Jadeja shared 9 wickets amongst themselves, with 3 apiece. To ensure that he does not get left out, Bhuvneshwar Kumar got a solitary wicket as well.

It was a good reply from the Kiwis this morning. Guptill and Latham added 55 for the opening wicket followed by a 49-run stand between Latham and Nicholls. At 135/3 during the Tea break, it seemed like this match would go into Day 5 but again, this is India.

A comfortable and comprehensive win for India. Matthew Hayden used to say on commentary - "There are times when you feel nothing is happening in a Test in India. Then suddenly the game turns." Something similar happened today.

Murali Vijay goes to his right from second slip and makes no mistake. The players shake hands. INDIA WIN BY 178 RUNS AND TAKE AN UNASSAILABLE 2-0 SERIES LEAD!

India get the breakthrough finally. Coming back to the ball, there was not enough turn and Nicholls failed to cover that line. Actually angle did the trick there for Jadeja.

In the air... but safe! Short of a length ball on middle and leg, Nicholls goes for the pull but gets a top edge. The ball lands safely near mid-wicket for a couple.

OUT! Gone this time! Ashwin bowls it full around the off stump line, Guptill brings his bat down to defend but it's jammed due to his front pad. As a result, Guptill is hit on the pads and there is a big appeal for a leg before wicket. Umpire Kettleborough raises his finger this time and India finally get a breakthrough. Ashwin strikes in the very first over after lunch. Guptill's poor form continues and he will be lucky to play the next Test.
APPEAL! Flighted around off, Guptill tries to defend but gets hit on the pads. Ashwin appeals confidently for bat-pad but the umpire says not out.

We are back for the afternoon session! Martin Guptill and Tom Latham are out in the middle. Ravichandran Ashwin to bowl.
...Day 4, Session 2...

New Zealand still have a mountain to climb as they have to bat out five more sessions to save this game. India will look to come back hard in the second session and pick some quick wickets. So join us back in a bit to catch the second session!

Pretty good session for the Kiwis! They've played out the tricky phase as they didn't lose a single wicket. First they bowled out the hosts when Wagner and Boult snared a wicket each and then the openers gave them a gritty start. The Indian bowlers tried their best but Latham and Guptill played to the merit of the ball and gave their side a cautious start.
Full on middle and off, Guptill flicks it behind square leg for a single. LUNCH ON DAY 4!
The batsman works it down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and outside off, Latham reaches out and drives it through the covers for a brace. Ravindra Jadeja cuts it off at point.

On middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a couple. 50 UP FOR NEW ZEALAND!

Beautiful shot. Tossed up outside off, Guptill leans and drives it through the covers. Virat Kohli dives from short extra cover, but misses. Bhuvneshwar Kumar dives too from cover but misses as well. The ball goes towards the ropes but Mohammed Shami chases it down from mid off. He gets to the ball, stops it, goes past the boundary, comes back and then returns the ball. Enough time to take three.
Full and wide outside off, Martin lunges out and slaps it towards short extra cover. Virat Kohli gets across, stops the ball and mimes a shy at the striker's end. Aggression.
Around off, watchfully kept out.

Time for spin. Early in this innings. RAVICHANDRAN ASHWIN comes on to bowl.

Time for a chat. Visibly, umpire Rod Tucker is not happy with the excessive bit of appealing going on out there. Almost every play and a miss and every ball hitting the pads is followed by an "AAAAAOUTT WAS THATTTTT!!!" and he is getting irritated. He calls Kohli and quietly warns him to keep the appealing in control.
On a good length outside off, Martin looks to defend but the ball shapes away to beat the outside edge. Saha appeals from behind, Kohli makes it more vociferous but the umpire is unmoved.
Full and outside off, driven down the ground. Ravichandran Ashwin gets across from mid on to stop the ball. A single taken.

HUGE APPEAL FOR LBW! The umpire says it is not out. The Indians are looking shocked. Full and outside off, Guptill looks to drive it straight down the ground but misses and is hit on the pads. Shami appeals but the umpire reckons an inside edge. The batsmen take a run as well as the ball goes to point. Replays do not detect any inside edge. That seemed like it will hit the leg stump.

Simon Doull on air says that Gautam Gambhir is on as a substitute for Shikhar Dhawan. The latter was hit a couple of times on the left thumb by Trent Boult while batting in the third innings. Doull further says that the news from the Indian camp is that it is not very serious and he has been rested for this innings as a precautionary measure. Remember, the third and final Test starts on Saturday. Not much time to recover.
